title: Teriyaki Salmon
subtitle: glazed salmon fillet in teriyaki sauce
excerpt: Teriyaki salmon is pan-seared salmon fillet glazed with a sweet soy sauce that caramelises in the pan. It takes about 15 minutes from start to plate. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Teriyaki is a Japanese cooking method where fish or meat is grilled or pan-fried and glazed with a sweet soy marinade. Salmon is the most popular home version because the fat in the fish works very well with the caramelised glaze.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be mixed up to 3 days ahead and kept in the fridge.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Japanese cooking method where protein is coated in a glaze of soy sauce, mirin and sugar and cooked until it caramelises. The name comes from 'teri' meaning shine and 'yaki' meaning grill.
Sweet Japanese rice wine. It provides the sweetness and shine that is essential to a teriyaki glaze.

content.text: method is fast and the results depend on heat control. Sear the salmon skin-side down first to crisp the skin, then flip and pour in the sauce, letting it bubble and caramelise around the fish.
gives the glaze its characteristic shine. Serves 4.
Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in two batches if your pan is smaller than 26cm so the salmon sears rather than steams.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar together in a small bowl. Set aside.
Pat the salmon fillets dry with kitchen paper. Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Place the salmon skin-side down and press gently with a spatula for the first 30 seconds.
Cook skin-side down for 4 minutes until the skin is very crispy and golden. Flip the salmon and cook flesh-side down for 2 minutes.
Pour the teriyaki sauce into the pan. It will bubble up quickly. Spoon the sauce over the salmon continuously for about 1 minute until it thickens to a glaze.
Transfer the salmon to plates. Spoon any remaining glaze from the pan over the top. Scatter with sesame seeds and spring onion and serve with steamed rice.

attrs.cause: Heat was too high when the sauce was added
attrs.fix: Reduce the heat to medium before pouring in the sauce. The sugar in the mirin burns quickly.

attrs.symptom: Salmon skin is soft and not crispy
attrs.cause: Pan was not hot enough or skin was wet when it went in
attrs.fix: Pat the skin completely dry before cooking. The pan needs to be very hot before the fish goes in.

attrs.cause: It was flipped too early before the skin released naturally
attrs.fix: Leave the salmon untouched for the full 4 minutes skin-side down. It will release cleanly when ready.

content.text: Teriyaki salmon is one of the most cooked Japanese dishes in home kitchens worldwide. The method works on chicken, mackerel and tofu as well. In Japan, teriyaki is a technique as much as a flavour. The shiny glaze is what sets it apart from a plain pan-fried piece of fish. Serve it with steamed rice and miso soup for a complete Japanese meal.
